text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- The government presented reforms to Austria's trade law after a closed meeting yesterday. An agreement on work laws was postponed.
- The newspaper reports that the consortium around EA-Generali will offer 10 billion schillings with Die Erste savings bank for the government's stake in Creditanstalt.
- Austria's middle sized firms are more optimistic for the future. However insolvencies will be worse in 1997, researcher Creditreform says.
- Austrian productivity has caught up with Germany's after it had been 23 percent behind only 15 years ago.
- Energy supplier EVN's pre-tax profit went up 24.4 percent to 1.5 billion schillings in 1995/96 due to the long winter. The dividend will be raised to 25 schillings.
- Upper Austrian engineer Elektro Bau AG (EBG) has received an order for all the electrotechnical engineering to make Swatch's Smart car.
DIE PRESSE
- Austria Tabak will be privatised in 1997, after investment banks have presented ideas on how to carry out the sale.
- Tension is high in Austria's metal industry after wage negotiations failed to bring a result.
KURIER

- Rudolf Gruber, president of Austria's electricity industry, has said that Austria's energy suppliers should work together more closely, so as to minimize the risks associated with the liberalisation of the market.
- Austria might earn one billion schillings more next year, should it privatise the stock exchange.
- Heavy winds of up to 170 km/h have caused major damage across wide parts of Austria.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- The newly introduced minimum corporate tax of 50,000 schillings might be overruled by Austria's constitutional court
- Finance MInister Viktor Klima plans to exclude 77 billion schillings worth of debts of motorway financer Asfinag from the government's budget.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Austria's farmers demand the government double EU-subisidies of 335 billion schillings for damages due to the BSE-crisis.
